labels.notes: colI_v1.tex l.766-768, with l(p) and Gamma_p from l.762-764. GX.GammaLinkCircle L has four fields: pt : HS 2; atlas : ChartedSpace (Link pt) L; hasGroupoid in gxGroupoid (GammaP pt) (Link pt), whose elements are locally the action of an element of the group (the standard (G,X)-groupoid, DEC-16); and isCircle : L homeomorphic to Circle. GX.Link p = RaySphere (Minkowski 2 / R p), the space of rays in T_[p] HS^2. The identification T_[p] S(V) = V/Rp is canonical up to positive scaling, so the rays are canonical. GX.GammaP p = {A in Causal.Flat.lorentz 2 | A p = p}. Here lorentz 2 is SO_0(1,2): linear, Q-preserving, future-preserving, det 1, as in HSModel's checklist. This is the pointwise stabiliser, the paper's choice (REVIEW Q2), not the full stabiliser. Gamma_p acts on l(p) by the induced map on V/Rp, which is the differential at [p] of [v] -> [Av]. No hypothesis is added, and nothing is vacuous: GammaLinkCircle.regular inhabits it with l(p) itself. Lean = paper. The mark is legitimate. None of the four readings touches the definition. The double-cover reading of the natural RP1-structure and the orientation convention concern l.770-771, which is unlabelled. The angle normalisation and 'elliptic includes central' concern l.688-744, also unlabelled. The definition mentions no RP1-structure, no orientation and no angle. Docstring citation colI_v1.tex:766 is correct, and the label lies within the first 4000 characters. The decls list attaches the l.770 theorems (rp1ChartedSpace, rp1_hasGroupoid, rp1_compatible) to this definition label, which is a curation choice for the master: under the doubledag principal rule they become principals, and GX.GammaLinkCircle becomes subordinate.

angle_normalisation_check: 4π for the link of a regular point is consistent with the paper's use of the angle. (i) l.742-744 do not normalise 'the angle'. (ii) The paper fixes the normalisation implicitly in Lemma surgery-key (l.2952-2969): 'C_+ carries an elliptic structure of angle θ' then embeds in P_θ, the model of a particle of cone angle θ (l.2791-2807). In the regular case θ = 2π, C_+ is the boundary of H^2, i.e. RP1 with holonomy δ. So angle(δ) = 2π: the closer's convention, and N4's (Θ < 2π for positive mass, M = 1 - Θ/2π). (iii) l.902-905 make one turn of l(p) equal to δ^2 at a space-like p: the components of I^+ are δ^{2i}]x0,x1[, and the degree is even. That forces the double-cover reading of l.770 wherever the sentence is read uniformly in p, and with it holonomy δ^2 and angle 4π for a regular link, as the closer proves (GX.hasLiftedHolonomy_link). (iv) The paper never gives a number for the RP1-angle of a link l(p). It says only that time-like singularities are 'characterized by' their elliptic RP1-circle (l.808-809) and 'by their cone angle' (l.864). Both hold when RP1-angle = 2 × cone angle. So nothing in the paper is contradicted. The factor 2 between a cone point's link (2θ) and the photon circle around it (θ) is real under the uniform reading, and the question to the author stands, refined by finding 4.

findings.what: False mathematical assertion addressed to the author. SCOPE (c) says 'opposite choices [of the orientations of HS^2 and RP1] exchange positive and negative circles (l.908-922)'. The REPORT question says 'The opposite orientation of HS^2 gives the mirror RP1-structure, and it exchanges positive and negative circles (l.908-922, Remark l.926)'. Both are false. Proof, with the closer's conventions. Reversing the orientation of HS^2 replaces θ by conj∘θ, so linkToRP1 becomes c∘linkToRP1, with c = conjugation and lift c~(t) = -t. The lifted developing map D becomes -D, which is decreasing. So the canonical orientation of l.729-731 (StrictMono in HasLiftedHolonomy) flips: D''(s) = -D(-s). The new lifted holonomy is f' = c~ f^{-1} c~. Since c~ δ^{-1} c~ = δ, f = δ^k g gives f' = δ^k g' with g' = c~ g^{-1} c~. The degree is unchanged, and so are the trace class and the angle. The new I^+ is -I^+, because i^+(l(p)) depends on the time orientation, not on the orientation of HS^2. For x in I^+: g'(-x) >= -x iff g^{-1}x <= x iff gx >= x. So a circle is positive (l.920: gx >= x on I^+) in the mirror iff it is positive in the original. A concrete check gives the same answer: p = e_{x0}, with the boost B_η in the (t, x1)-plane and degree 2; the circle is negative for η > 0 under both orientations. Reversing the order of RP1~ (l.676) also preserves positivity, because δ, γ_0 and g all invert together. The parabolic classes of l.745-752 are preserved too. Moreover, f' has the same invariants as f (k, |tr|, sign, or τ), so by the classification of l.701-760 the mirror RP1-circle is RP1-isomorphic to the original. The orientation convention changes no invariant of the underlying RP1-circle. The orientation question as posed to the author rests on a false stake. The error would also enter the strict library's documentation, since the REPORT proposes to graduate the file 'as is'.
findings.fix: Text only, no Lean change. In SCOPE (c) and in the REPORT question, replace the clause with: 'the opposite orientation of HS^2 (or of RP1~) gives the mirror RP1-structure. Its lifted holonomy is c~ f^{-1} c~ = δ^k (c~ g^{-1} c~) and its I^± are -I^±, so the degree, the angle, the trace class and the sign (positive/negative, l.908-922) are unchanged.' Then reduce the orientation question to the convention itself, or drop it. Optionally, prove the invariance in Lean: it is short with HasLiftedHolonomy.

findings.what: The docstring says 'The sentence after it (l.770-771) is proved too', and Main declarations presents 'the natural RP1-structure of l(p) = the double covering S(T_pHS^2) -> P(T_pHS^2)' as fact. The REPORT, by contrast, records it as a 'Reading taken' (labels[0].questions[0]). SCOPE (a)-(d) list the angle, orientation and 'elliptic' readings but not this one. The reading is well supported: l.902-905 force it at space-like p, and at light-like p no equivariant homeomorphism l(p) -> RP1 exists (two Gamma_p-fixed points against one). It is still a reading, and the docstring contract (lean-causal kb 0006, item 5) asks SCOPE to disclose it. This does not affect the mark: the sentence is unlabelled.
findings.fix: Add a SCOPE item: '(e) l.770's natural RP1-structure is read as the double cover S(T_pHS^2) -> P(T_pHS^2) ~ RP1 through an oriented θ (evidence: l.902-905, one turn of l(p) is δ^2)'. Qualify l.17 with 'under that reading'.

findings.what: The HasLiftedHolonomy docstring and the REPORT say 'f x > x on the image of the developing map (eq>, GX.HasLiftedHolonomy.lt_apply)'. lt_apply proves only `∃ x, x < f x`. The statement on the whole image is true and immediate (D StrictMono, D(s+1) = f(D s)), but no declaration states it, and the cited one is weaker than the sentence.
findings.fix: Either reword the docstring and the REPORT to 'f x > x at some (indeed every) point of the image', or state the image version: from the witnesses E, D, ∀ s, D s < f (D s).

findings.what: The question offers only one way out of the factor 2: renormalise δ = π, which makes the photon circle of H^2 angle π. It omits two facts the author needs. (a) The paper already fixes angle(δ) = 2π through Lemma surgery-key (l.2952-2969 with P_θ, l.2791-2807), not only through NOTES-3+1 N4. SCOPE's 'the angle of l.744 is not normalised by the paper' is true of l.744 but not of the paper. (b) At a time-like p there is a second natural, Gamma_p-equivariant RP1-structure on l(p). The visual map v -> endpoint of c_v on ∂H^2_+ ~ RP1 (via SO_0(1,2) ≈ PSL(2,R), l.763) has degree one. Under it a regular link has holonomy δ and angle 2π, a cone point's link has angle θ = its cone angle, and Gamma_p maps into G by the inclusion, as l.786-787 says. It does not exist at space-like or light-like p: there Gamma_p fixes 4 or 2 rays, while a non-trivial element of PSL(2,R) fixes at most 2 points of RP1, and a parabolic one only 1. So the double cover is the only uniform reading, but the factor 2 could also be resolved by a p-dependent reading, not only by renormalising. The closer's [r] statement ('no degree-one equivariant identification at a space-like p') is correct as stated.
findings.fix: Add (a) and (b) to the question, so that the author chooses among: uniform double cover with angle(link) = 2 × cone angle (the formalized one); the visual structure at time-like p; or renormalising δ = π.
